extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and HWA members submitting or promoting works for the Bram Stoker Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidelines for submitting works to the Bram Stoker Awards and for acceptable/unacceptable promotion of those works (including jury submissions, member recommendations, linking, mass emails, and social-media announcements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting vs Soliciting
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in mind the difference between promoting and soliciting. Promoting (acceptable) is the business of spreading the word about your work and making sure anyone who wants to can read it. Soliciting (unacceptable) is the practice of wheeling and dealing, whining and wheedling, in order to get yourself an award that you may not deserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works truly worthy of the award tend to rise to the top without help if enough people read them. If you have to beg for recommendations or votes, that reflects poorly on you and the work; refrain from soliciting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBLICIZE
rubrics_metrics.description: The very best way to promote a book for a Bram Stoker Award® is to publicize the book as widely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most HWA members who participate in the process are voracious readers and subscribe to magazines, newsletters, and websites that offer reviews and ads for horror-related material. Use usual publicity channels to reach reviewers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: REVIEWS / reviewer list
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an HWA member, you might find our list of horror reviewers useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the list in the Members-Only section of the website to identify reviewers and outlets that might cover your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising in the HWA Newsletter
rubrics_metrics.description: You or your publisher may take out an advertisement for a book in the HWA Newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may NOT solicit for award recognition in the ad, including the use of phrases such as 'For Your Consideration.' See the Newsletter Ad Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Release Announcement (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an HWA member, you may notify the organization of your new release and have notices placed in several places in our publications, free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places include: a notice in 'Fiendish Endeavors' or 'Recently Born of Horrific Minds' sections of the HWA Newsletter, New Releases blog posts, and a notice in the regular Internet Mailer. Use the Members-Only 'Promote Yourself' link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer your work to the Jury – follow category guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to submit your work for Jury consideration, you must follow the special guidelines on these pages for each category (Anthology, Collection, First Novel, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may only submit ONE WORK per form. Multiple short stories must be submitted individually because the system submits and tracks each work separately. Multiple submissions on one form may cause works to be missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred format for Jury submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital copies are strongly preferred for Jury submissions; hard copies make dissemination to jurors difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a hard copy only as a last resort if no digital copy exists. For hard copy submissions, email stokerchair@horror.org to get the mailing address. The organization cannot absolutely guarantee delivery of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury submission final deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The cutoff date and time for all Jury submissions is 11:59PM (Pacific Standard Time) on November 30th each calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deadline gives Juries time to read and deliver Recommendations by January 15. Exception: works published between December 1–31 may be submitted by 11:59PM on December 31st (PST). Works published prior to November 30 but submitted after November 30 will NOT be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for December publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you expect your work to be published in December you should try to submit a PDF or MS of the work to the Jury Chair prior to 30 November.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any work that will be published in December will likely already be in manuscript form that the Jury could review; submitting earlier increases chances of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members' Recommendation process deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Members' Recommendation process is separate from the Jury submission ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works can still be Recommended by individual members using that process until January 15th of the following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking a recommended work – who may supply links
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the author, author's agent, or publisher of a recommended work may request that a link to where the member can access more information on the work be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links allowed include: a web address where the reader can download the work for free, the Amazon.com sales page, the publisher’s website, the author's webpage showcasing the work, or an email address where the reader can request a free copy. You do not have to be an HWA member to activate your link, but the work must appear on the members-only recommendations page or the Bram Stoker Awards® Reading List first.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request link activation
rubrics_metrics.description: If your work has received a recommendation, you may supply the Compiler with a URL or email address for linking and ask that your link be activated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may verify posting via the Members-Only Bram Stoker Awards page; non-members check the Bram Stoker Awards® Reading List and contact the Compiler at compiler@horror.org if the work appears there and they wish to provide a link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the Member Directory / Opt-In Promo Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: HWA members can access the Member Directory of all HWA members willing to receive promotional material; read the warning message about proper use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Members Opt-In Promo Materials' list in the Members-Only section and respect members' preferences; do not misuse the list to solicit recommendations or votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-In Email — one mass email per work
rubrics_metrics.description: You may send ONE mass email consisting only of an 'offering' for the work(s) you would like considered for the awards year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have multiple works you may send one mass email for each work but it's suggested to offer all works in a single email. You may only respond to members who have 'opted in' to receive your materials; do not follow up asking for thoughts, reviews, or votes. Use BCC when sending mass mailings. Correct terminology: 'I/we am/are offering a copy of this work to you for Bram Stoker Award® consideration.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Building the Opt-In mailing list (Wild Apricot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for creating a mailing list from the live Members Opt-In Promo Materials page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the page's 'Show' pulldown to display all entries, copy the page, paste into Excel (columns recognized), and pull information immediately before sending because the list updates in real time. Be aware some members want direct sends, some want to be queried first, others only want to review for the Bram Stoker Awards. ALWAYS use BCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-In communications etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not follow-up with the members whom you've sent your work to, asking for their thoughts on your work, to leave you a review for the work, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-In members are expected not to reply to authors who have sent their work for consideration. Never use the Directory to solicit recommendations or votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facebook announcement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may post one (and only one) promotional announcement about each of your eligible works at the HWA Facebook group; award consideration announcements may be posted only on Saturdays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the announcement to supply a contact where people can find out more or obtain the work; discourage posting direct links to the work(s) and DO NOT post the text of your story. The HWA Facebook group is currently the ONLY acceptable place to post an opt-in offer on social media; no other social media announcement or post is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary and Final Ballot Mailer confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Internet Mailer will be sent to members with summaries and links offered for download from works appearing on the Preliminary and Final Ballots; these links are intended for voting members only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links are not to be shared by unauthorized persons. Works are copyrighted; sharing links without permission is theft and may result in dismissal from the organization and possible legal action. If your work appears on the ballots you may place a notice in the special ballot issue telling members how to obtain a copy (contact imailer@horror.org before the announced deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing copies on request only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only provide copies if members have requested your work through promotional offerings listed here as acceptable practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Via Email: provide free copies only to HWA members who requested one after your promotional offering. Do not follow up with members asking for feedback or reviews. Remember copyright: works provided for consideration may not be passed on to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: When you may claim 'Nominee' status
rubrics_metrics.description: You may mention that your work has appeared on the Bram Stoker Awards® preliminary or final ballot, but you may not promote your work as 'Bram Stoker Recommended' unless it appears on the FINAL ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that appear on the Preliminary Ballot are NOT Bram Stoker Award nominees. Only FINAL ballot appearance permits promotion as a nominee. In the case of an Anthology on the FINAL Ballot, editor(s) may promote themselves as nominees/finalists, but individual contributing authors may state they have a story in a nominated anthology — they are not nominees themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonest or deceptive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not engage in dishonest or deceptive practices, including recommending works you have not read, trading recommendations with others, and soliciting Bram Stoker Award® recommendations from friends and acquaintances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complying with such requests is equally unacceptable. Such behavior degrades the process and harms the awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: No soliciting recommendations or votes (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not solicit Bram Stoker Award® recommendations or votes. And if you are an HWA member, you may not comply with any such request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Recommendations process is anonymous (Rule VIn); publicizing your Recommendations is a breach of that Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: No direct contact with Jurors / no spamming the Jury
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not spam the Jury or contact Jurors about your work outside the published process of 'What Is Acceptable' above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spamming will most likely render your work ineligible for Bram Stoker Award® consideration. After submission you will receive only an acknowledgment; under no circumstances email asking how the jury liked your work, if they read it, or if they will include it in their selection. Continued contact may render the work ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited promotional contact
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not send unsolicited emails or other forms of contact (such as Twitter) promoting your work for a Bram Stoker Award®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited emails that include PDFs or other attachments are particularly unacceptable and hurt your cause; receiving junk or unrequested attached files angers people and damages reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on HWA Internet Mailer Bram Stoker announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond your one new release announcement, you may not post additional Bram Stoker Award-related announcements in regular editions of the HWA Internet Mailer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bram Stoker Award-related announcements are limited to the special 'Preliminary Ballot' and 'Final Ballot' issues of the Mailer. Only works that appear on those ballots are eligible for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion rules for collections vs individual stories
rubrics_metrics.description: You may promote individual stories from a fiction collection in the post promoting the collection; however, you may not post separate promotions for both a collection and individual stories from that collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multiple separate promotions for the same underlying eligible work(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Message board posting limits and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not post the text of your story on the HWA message board, and you may not post more than one Bram Stoker Award® promo announcement per year per eligible work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements should be used to supply links to locations where people can obtain the work or find out more about it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misrepresent Recommendation/Reading List status
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not promote your work as 'Bram Stoker Award Recommended' nor as appearing on the Bram Stoker Award Reading List unless that status is accurate (Receiving a small number of recommendations does not equal being a nominee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promoting such limited recognition devalues the Awards and may offend voting members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect copyrights of materials provided for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Works submitted to members for Bram Stoker Awards® consideration are copyrighted and are provided for the sole purpose of considering their merit for Member Recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pass on copies to other parties. If someone requests you to pass on a copy you should refuse and direct complaints to president@horror.org. HWA supports protecting copyright rights of members and authors.
